A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SmoothSA work, with readable text, equations, tables and figures. The complete eight-page v2 has no appendix; v3 includes readable Appendices A–B. The material supports comparison despite some ambiguous experimental descriptions.

before.justification: v2 reports original object-discovery, object-recognition, VQA and ablation results, including Tables 1–5 and Figure 4.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical evaluations and adds video benchmarks, computation measurements, corruption experiments and contraction diagnostics, including Appendices A–B.

M1.justification: The preheater architecture, attention order, stop-gradient/MSE objective and shared three-plus-one iteration procedure match. However, v2 explicitly removes DIAS self-distillation when constructing SmoothSAi, whereas v3 mentions removing only slot pruning. The PDFs do not establish whether this omission denotes a changed method component or shortened documentation.

E1.justification: v3 adds conditional MOVi-D and MOVi-E video discovery and YTVIS-2022 discovery and recognition. MOVi-C was already evaluated in v2's conditional ablation, so its expanded benchmark reporting is not a newly introduced dataset. YTVIS-HQ corresponds to v2's explicitly identified high-quality YTVIS.

E2.justification: Table 2 drops DIASv from the YTVIS/HQ comparison. STEVE, mentioned in both versions but lacking a reported comparison row in v2, receives MOVi-D results in v3. The image, recognition and VQA comparator rosters otherwise remain.

E3.justification: Recognition evaluation replaces bounding-box R2 with IoU and adds top-3 accuracy and matched-object counts. Figure 4 changes its aggregate from ARI+ARIfg to the sum of all four discovery metrics. New corruption and computation experiments introduce additional protocols. Resolution captions change from '256×256 (224×224)' to '224×224', without establishing which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond v2's iteration-count analyses, v3 adds segmentation trajectories and feature-gradient visualizations in Figure 4, measured computation costs in Table 6, a severe slot-corruption stress test in Appendix A, and iteration-distance diagnostics at training checkpoints in Appendix B. These investigate mechanisms, robustness and efficiency previously untested in these forms.

E5.justification: Both versions already specify three random seeds and report results with uncertainty values. Appendix A newly identifies seeds 42, 43 and 44. No increased repeat count or new significance-testing procedure is established.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 substantially revise and expand results: for example, reported SmoothSAi COCO ARI changes from 26.2 to 29.3. Recognition scores are replaced alongside metric changes, preventing direct cross-version performance claims. New video, computation, corruption and contraction results appear; Table 5 adds a no-preheater result of 56.9±2.5. Table 4's VQA results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v3 Section 3.1 adds contraction assumptions, a Banach fixed-point argument and preheating error bounds in Equations 3–7, plus Jacobian bounds and a gradient derivation in Equations 10–15. These go substantially beyond v2's procedural equations and intuitive motivation. Appendix B qualifies the contraction interpretation rather than supplying a global guarantee.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same core contributions: addressing query cold-start and transform homogeneity, achieving state-of-the-art object discovery, and improving downstream tasks. The added analyses and benchmarks support these retained claims without introducing a distinct core contribution.

C2.justification: v3 adds fixed-point, gradient-balance and feature-anchoring explanations and revises the computation-overhead discussion. Its limitations replace v2's fixed-slot-count problem with poor-slot feedback and the potentially unsuitable fixed three-plus-one schedule. Appendix A argues robustness to corrupted slots, while Appendix B explicitly limits the contraction interpretation to illustrative motivation.

D1.justification: The supplement-only code statement becomes repository access information claiming source code, checkpoints and training logs. v3 adds V100 timing/memory measurements, batch sizes, the gradient-map calculation and a corruption recipe specifying strength 0.999 and 1,000 interventions across 100,000 training steps. Conversely, Table 3 drops v2's '#step=20' annotation. Resource availability was not externally verified.

R1.justification: v3 removes the Oquab et al. DINOv2 citation and reference. It also drops v2's explicit acknowledgment that MetaSlot effectively mitigates cold-start, emphasizing instead that previous methods did not address it explicitly. The overall first-explicit-solution positioning and remaining cited works are largely retained.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work and method prose undergo substantial condensation and rewriting, while the discussion is extensively recast around mechanisms. v3 introduces numbered sections and subsections, formalism boxes, an impact statement and appendices, substantially changing the exposition despite retaining the main section sequence.

P2.justification: v3 changes the page template and adds boxed formalism, expanded multi-dataset Tables 2–3, Table 6 and appendix tables. Figure 4 becomes a wide composite of curves, segmentations and gradient maps instead of a single plot. Figures 1–2 gain annotations; Figure 3 retains the same qualitative examples. Tables 2–3 also contain explicit update blocks.

improvement.justification: Broader video evaluation, robustness diagnostics and resource measurements make v3 more informative. However, its new fixed-point argument infers that the preheated run is closer by comparing upper bounds, which does not establish that ordering; Appendix B's qualification does not repair this inference. Table 3 also reports worse SmoothSAv video box IoU than SlotContrast, including 42.6 versus 51.5 on YTVIS-HQ, without discussing this tradeoff alongside retained broad benefit claims. These validation gains and reliability problems leave the net quality direction uncertain.
